newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stock exchange to join working group on "bugs".
newsitem.headline: HK stock exchange to join working group on "bugs".

text.p: The Hong Kong Stock Exchange said on Monday that it would join a working group to handle incidents like a software bug last year that skewed exchange closing price quotations.
"The importance of providing a smooth and efficient trading environment cannot be overemphasised," the stock exchange said in a report to the Legislative Council's panel on financial affairs.
The stock exchange said it had called in Andersen Consulting to review the incident, identify its causes and define corrective and preventive measures for the future.

Andersen recommended the development of a comprehensive framework for contingency management to handle incidents involving major market institutions including the Hong Kong Securities Clearing Company, the stock exchange, the Hong Kong Futures Exchange and Hang Seng Index Services (HSIS), it said.
The stock exchange said it would actively take part in "an intermarket contingency working group" organised by the Securities and Futures Commission.
In the December 12 glitch, a software bug caused the wrong closing prices for the previous day to be shown on stock exchange computer screens.
As a result, the misquotes caused the blue chip Hang Seng Index to appear to plunge about 515 points or nearly four percent in the opening minutes of trade.
The day's low was later found to be just 158 points down.
The exchange said HSIS would handle similar incidents to the December 12 glitch in future.
HSIS is charged with calculating the Hang Seng Index based on prices provided by the stock exchange.
